title: Meinhard made bishop of Livonia
description: The missionary Meinhard, who had built a stone church at Ikšķile, is consecrated the first bishop of Livonia.

title: Riga founded
description: Bishop Albert moves his seat to the mouth of the Daugava and founds Riga as the base of the Livonian crusade.

title: Livonian Brothers of the Sword founded
description: Bishop Albert founds an order of crusading knights, which conquers much of present-day Latvia and Estonia before merging into the Teutonic Order.

title: Riga joins the Hanseatic League
description: Riga becomes a member of the Hanseatic League, which shapes its trade for three centuries.

title: Livonian Confederation agreed
description: The Livonian Order, the bishops and the towns sign a pact binding the lands of Livonia into a confederation.

title: Reformation reaches Riga
description: Lutheran preaching begins in the churches of Riga, and the town soon adopts the new faith.

title: Treaty of Vilnius
description: The Livonian Order is dissolved and its lands pass to Poland–Lithuania, with its last master becoming Duke of Courland.

title: Sweden takes Riga
description: Gustavus Adolphus captures Riga, which becomes the largest city in the Swedish realm.

title: Courland colony on Tobago
place: Great Courland Bay, Trinidad and Tobago
description: Settlers sent by Duke Jacob Kettler found a colony on Tobago, the best known overseas venture of the small duchy.

title: Bible printed in Latvian
description: The pastor Johann Ernst Glück's translation of the whole Bible is published, setting a standard for written Latvian.

title: Riga surrenders to Russia
description: After a siege made worse by plague, Riga capitulates to the army of Peter the Great and Swedish Livonia becomes Russian.

title: Courland annexed by Russia
description: In the Third Partition of Poland the Duchy of Courland passes to the Russian Empire, which now holds all of present-day Latvia.

title: Serfdom abolished in Livonia
description: Peasants in the Governorate of Livonia are freed from serfdom without land, two years after those of Courland.

title: First Latvian Song Festival
description: Choirs gather in Riga for the first all-Latvian song festival, a landmark of the national awakening.

title: Revolution of 1905
description: Troops fire on demonstrators in Riga, and the unrest grows into a revolt against both Russian rule and the Baltic German landowners.

title: Independence proclaimed
description: The People's Council proclaims the Republic of Latvia in what is now the National Theatre.

title: Battle of Cēsis
description: Estonian and Latvian troops defeat the Baltic German Landeswehr, a victory Estonia marks as Victory Day.

title: Bermondt's army driven from Riga
description: Latvian forces push the German-backed West Russian Volunteer Army away from Riga, a day kept as Lāčplēsis Day.

title: Peace treaty with Soviet Russia
description: Soviet Russia recognises Latvian independence and gives up all claims to its territory.

title: Ulmanis coup
description: Prime Minister Kārlis Ulmanis dissolves parliament and the parties and rules as an authoritarian leader.

title: Soviet occupation
description: The Red Army occupies Latvia after an ultimatum, and the country is annexed to the Soviet Union in August.

title: June deportation
description: Soviet security forces deport tens of thousands of people from the Baltic states and other annexed lands to Siberia and Kazakhstan.

title: Rumbula massacre
description: On two days German forces and Latvian auxiliaries shoot about 25,000 Jews, most of them from the Riga Ghetto.

title: Declaration restoring independence
description: The Supreme Council declares the 1940 annexation illegal and begins a transition to full independence.

title: The Barricades
description: Unarmed civilians barricade key buildings in Riga against Soviet forces, and several people are killed.

title: Full independence
description: During the coup attempt in Moscow the Supreme Council ends the transition period and declares Latvia fully independent.

title: Latvia joins the European Union
description: Latvia enters the European Union, a month after joining NATO.
